doc.title: Buster Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002

title: How he composes, and the origin of Christina
summary: He says tunes can start anywhere and describes writing Christina for his sister's newborn daughter.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Let me just ask you briefly about your compositions. Do you write at the piano? Do you start from your bass? How does a tune start for you?

It may come from anywhere. It may start on the piano, it may start on the bass, it may start in a dream. But someone said something very interesting and that was as far as composing, try not to compose from the piano because you stand a chance of being limited by your ability to play the piano. But nevertheless, an idea can come from wherever. One of my most-liked tunes it seems is “Christina.” And “Christina” came from a request from my sister to write a song for her newborn daughter. So the song was inspired by this little girl’s vibe, persona, whatever. And it turns out that it’s one that works real well. But yeah, it can come from — but at some point I’ve got to sit down at the piano and figure it out. It’s not important for me to be able to play it. It’s important for me to be able to write it. And then I can get the piano player to play it.
